newsitem.title: CHINA: China wheat shortfall seen 10 mln T in 2000.
newsitem.headline: China wheat shortfall seen 10 mln T in 2000.

text.p: China is expected to have a shortfall of about 10 million tonnes of wheat a year by the year 2000, the Futures Herald said in an edition seen in Beijing on Friday.
China's wheat demand was forecast at 110-125 million tonnes in 2000, the newspaper quoted agricultural expert Lu Ming as saying. Wheat output was expected to total 100.8-118.8 million tonnes.
The Wednesday edition of the newspaper quoted Lu as saying land under wheat should be maintained at above 28 million hectares (69 million acres).
Lu called on agricultural authorities to boost output per hectare under wheat and total wheat output, the newspaper said.
He urged southern Chinese provinces to expand land under wheat, it said.
